A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ctrl-Z Sampling and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Existing content can be matched reliably across the added sections, renumbering, and page moves.

before.justification: v4 reports original text-to-image benchmark results, ablations, sampler-integration experiments, and qualitative trajectory analyses in Section 5 and Appendices C and F.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds COCO diversity measurements and comparisons against additional inference-time methods.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the reward-plateau trigger, adaptive inversion-depth search, and candidate selection remain unchanged. The DPM/AYS and CFG++ integrations in v5 Appendix C.5 already appeared in v4 Appendix C.4.

E1.justification: v5 adds evaluation on a 2,000-image COCO subset in Section 5.4. This extends the represented image distribution within the existing text-to-image task; Pick-a-Pic, DrawBench, and T2I-CompBench coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New Appendix C.4 and Table 8 evaluate Best-of-N, Diffusion Tree Sampling, classical-search-based diffusion inference scaling (DIS), and Diffusion Alignment as Sampling (DAS), each at lower and higher budgets. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparison methods beyond v4's retained baselines; earlier citations to these approaches did not constitute these comparisons.

E3.justification: The new COCO experiment evaluates DDIM and two Ctrl-Z configurations using FID, precision, recall, and LPIPS. Appendix C.4 also introduces additional baseline comparisons around three and eight NFEs per sampling step. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds a focused analysis of whether reward-guided sampling sacrifices diversity through concentration on high-scoring outputs. Table 4 supplies distributional and perceptual measurements addressing that question. Existing depth, width, threshold, initiation, scheduling, and trajectory analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 3's statement about using the same prompts and seeds. v5 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Its discussion of multiple initial noise seeds describes population sampling rather than statistical replication.

E6.justification: Existing scores are unchanged, but Tables 4 and 8 substantially extend the findings. On COCO, DDIM versus Ctrl-Z‡ gives FID 40.22 versus 39.98, precision 71.20 versus 75.10, and recall 55.85 versus 55.20. The added comparisons reveal mixed rankings: DIS‡ reports ImageReward 1.186 at 8.00 NFEs, versus Ctrl-Z‡'s retained 1.138 at 7.72 NFEs. These are new comparisons, not improvements between versions under identical settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and their mathematical substance are retained, including the DDIM, inversion, acceptance, and CFG++ formulations. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations accompany the added empirical analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive exploration, escaping surrogate-quality plateaus, model compatibility, and compute–quality trade-offs. The new experiments do not redefine those core contributions.

C2.justification: v5 interprets gains on non-optimized reward metrics as evidence beyond scorer maximization. Section 5.4 attributes near-preserved diversity to bounded trajectory selection, while Appendix C.4 distinguishes single-latent refinement from population-based scaling. The existing limitations concerning reward scheduling and moderate evaluation budgets remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a code-repository link. Section 5.3 explicitly clarifies that evaluation metrics other than the selected surrogate reward are held out from exploration, documenting the existing experiment rather than establishing a procedural change. Existing hardware, software, and implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds four cited works: Gotta Hear Them All, Through the Magnifying Glass, LaVin-DiT, and AccelAES. Appendix C.4 also positions Ctrl-Z as complementary to population-based inference scaling. The established related-work narrative is otherwise largely unchanged; reference renumbering and removed bibliographic URLs are presentation edits.

P1.justification: v5 inserts Sample Diversity Analysis and Additional Baseline Comparisons subsections, renumbers subsequent subsections, and makes limited introduction, grammar, and author-information edits. Most existing prose, including the method and conclusion, is retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v5 adds Tables 4 and 8 for diversity and additional baselines. Existing tables are renumbered and displays move with text reflow, while Figures 1–12 retain their content. Bibliographic back-reference page links are removed, without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v5 improves empirical coverage by examining diversity loss and directly comparing four additional inference-time methods, including reporting competitors' stronger results on some metrics. The code-access pointer also improves transparency. The benefit is limited: the added studies use only Stable Diffusion 2.1, provide sparse details for reproducing the new evaluations, and report no uncertainty estimates. These are useful extensions to an otherwise unchanged paper.
